discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems and the Mott metal-insulator transition

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France, Paris / Flatiron Institute, New York

motivation: Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt created dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). Vollhardt and Metzner introduced the limit of infinite dimensions, and Georges and Kotliar mapped the lattice problem onto a self-consistent quantum impurity. Together these gave the first controlled, non-perturbative description of the Mott metal-insulator transition. DMFT predicted a first-order transition line ending at a critical point, the coexistence of quasiparticle and Hubbard bands, and bad-metal transport. Experiments on V2O3 and on organic κ-(BEDT-TTF)2X conductors confirmed these predictions strikingly, including Mott criticality, phase separation and optical spectral-weight transfer. Combined with density-functional theory, DMFT is now the standard tool for computing real correlated materials such as transition-metal oxides, actinides and iron-based superconductors. It changed how the whole field understands electron correlation.
